q-74629:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -12 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 16 & -9 & 4 \\ 2 & 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -12 & 12 & -4 \\ 5 & 16 & -9 & 4 \\ 2 & 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 16 & -9 & 4 \\ 2 & 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -21 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-21z=4 \\ y+6z=-1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=21z+4 \\ y=-6z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}21z+4 \\ -6z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-74626:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ -3 & -6 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -10 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-10z=-1 \\ y+4z=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=10z-1 \\ y=1-4z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10z-1 \\ 1-4z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-131647:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 4 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 4 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -8 & 6 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -6 & 12 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-33655:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,4)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩ \\ ⟨{t}^{4},\,{t}^{2},\,4t⟩ & =⟨1,\,1,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}{t}^{4}=1 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ 4t=4.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, we get $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(1,1,4)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$  

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2t,\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3},\,2(1),\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(1,1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨4,\,2,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{1}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

q-33584:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)\,j+y(t)\,j+z(t)\,k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by 

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(2,1,1)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+t\,k & =2\,i+\,j+\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ {t}^{2}=1 \\ t=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=1.$ This value satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, the point $P(2,1,1)$ is at the tip of $r(1).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at $P(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(1)}{‖{r}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\,i+2\,j+\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{2}{3}\,j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

q-32247:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now  

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+10{x}_{3}=-8 \\  & {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ and we have one free variable, ${x}_{3}.$ That means we need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ in terms of ${x}_{3}.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=-8-10{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}=6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}={x}_{3},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{3}$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8-10{x}_{3} \\ 6+6{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-42019:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=0 \\  & y-z=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=0 \\ y=z-1 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ z-1 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

q-131719:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 8 & -2 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

q-74634:
To classify the system, we will first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=\frac{9}{2},$ and it has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement III is true.
